newsitem.title: USA: Compaq sets five-for-two stock split.
newsitem.headline: Compaq sets five-for-two stock split.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp. on Tuesday announced a five-for-two stock split in the form of a stock dividend, fueling more investor optimism in the world's leading seller of personal computers.
Stock in the Houston-based company jumped as investors viewed the move as a bullish signal for Compaq's future.
"This stock split reflects our confidence in Compaq's long-term growth," Compaq Chairman Ben Rosen said in a statement.

Compaq stock closed up $2.375 at $101.875 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange amid a drop in other leading technology shares, as earnings jitters continued to roil computer stocks. Cyrix Corp. said late Monday it would report an unexpected second-quarter loss.
Cyrix, which develops clones of Intel Corp. microprocessors, cited weak overall demand and pricing pressures on its non-multimedia technology processors.

"Psychologically, (the stock split) does have an impact," said Walter Winnitzki, a PaineWebber Inc. analyst. "It relays the confidence that management has in the future. ... But realistically it shouldn't mean anything."
Compaq's move to split its shares also follows other leading technology companies, including its rival Dell Computer Corp., which announced a two-for-one split in May.
When Gateway 2000 Inc. announced its move to the NYSE in May, it also announced a two-for-one stock split. Intel Corp. and International Business Machines Corp. also split their shares.
Compaq has had two other stock splits. The first was a two-for-one in 1990 and the second a three-for-one in 1994.
Shareholders of record as of July 14 will receive three additional shares of common stock for every two shares they own on that date, Compaq said.
The new shares will be distributed on or about July 28.
Compaq said it had 276 million shares outstanding as of Monday. Upon completion of the split, the number will increase to 690 million shares outstanding.
In addition, the number of shares that would be issued in the recently announced proposed merger with Tandem Computers Inc. would be appropriately adjusted to reflect the stock split, Compaq said.
Wall Street analysts said the stock split will simply drive more retail interest in Compaq.

"Companies like to have their stock trade at prices that are attractive to various levels of investors," said Mark Specker, a SoundView Financial analyst. "It really doesn't have any significance at all."

Daniel Ries, a Nomura Research analyst said he was a bit surprised that Compaq split its stock five-for-two, instead of the typical two-for-one, but he added this will also fuel further retail interest.

Analysts also said Compaq stock was likely buoyant Tuesday because Compaq is one of the few technology companies that is expected to beat Wall Street forecasts this quarter, in an otherwise disappointing second quarter so far.
"I think it will comfortably exceed expectations," said Specker, adding that if Compaq just met expectations, Wall Street would be disappointed.
In 1996, Compaq earned $1.3 billion on worldwide sales of $18.1 billion. Compaq will report its second quarter earnings July 10.

Many technology companies have pre-announced earnings shortfalls this quarter, beginning with Intel, which cited weaker-than-expected demand, especially in Europe. Intel's warning was followed by disk drive maker Seagate Technology Inc., Gateway 2000 and Cyrix.
